newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWEAN SHARES CONTINUE WEAK ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWEAN SHARES CONTINUE WEAK ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded weaker on the back of further profit-taking on Thursday with brokers expecting the trend to continue into the next week.
The key industrial index lost 10.68 points to close at 12,048.28.
"The market saw some profit-taking again today and came off a bit. I think it will continue going down next week as well," one broker said.

Thursday's losers included agricultural investors Chemco who tumbled 400 cents to 4,200 while cable makers BICC CAFCA shed 70 cents to 250, tea growers Tanganda were down 50 cents at 800 and regional conglomerate TZI fell 20 cents to 925.
Other counters to trade weaker were plate and glass firm PGI which lost 20 cents to 490 while sugar growers Hippo eased 15 cents to 1,785.

Minings were quiet with gold producers Rio Tinto and coal giants Wankie at previous levels but Falgold, another gold firm, edged up 4 cents to 80. The secondary mining index inched up 2.02 points to close at 900.19.
